Reconstructed the path-decomposition, grouped rounding, rational-certificate, discrepancy, integrality, and special-case arguments from the exact target definitions.
Checked the Hoeffding and conditional-expectation constants symbolically, including bit-model implementability.
Created and ran the exact-arithmetic checker <workspace-home>/paired_targeted_stress_v2_scratch/targeted_icalp_unsplittable_two_sided/audit-revision/plain/iter_3/audit_exact_checks.py.

claims.claim: Every rational input flow x has a polynomial-size rational source-to-sink path decomposition, whose total weight q_st for each ordered pair (s,t) satisfies q_st<=d_t<=d_max.
claims.evidence: Add a supersource arc of value b(s) to each source and a sink-to-supersink arc of value d_t. The augmented flow is conserved at every original vertex and remains acyclic. Repeatedly subtracting the minimum residual value on a positive supersource-to-supersink path permanently zeros at least one arc, so at most |A|+|S+|+|S-| paths are produced. Polynomially many rational subtractions preserve polynomial encoding length. Removing auxiliary arcs gives the required paths; all weights terminating at t sum to d_t, so every nonnegative subtotal q_st is at most d_t<=d_max.
claims.search_method: Constructive augmented-flow proof with path-count and rational bit-length accounting.

claims.claim: After fixing the pair weights q_st, choosing one supported path P_st for every positive pair and assigning it weight q_st always produces a nonnegative unsplittable b-transshipment.
claims.evidence: A weighted s-to-t path has divergence +q_st at s, -q_st at t, and zero internally. The grouped decomposition gives row sums b(s) and column sums d_t, so summing any one selected path per positive pair preserves b. All weights are nonnegative and there is exactly one path for each positive ordered pair.

claims.claim: On rational inputs, any real feasible unsplittable solution can be replaced by one with polynomially bounded rational encoding; consequently, existence is in NP.
claims.evidence: Fix the at-most-one path chosen for each pair in a real solution. Its at most |S+||S-| weights satisfy rational row/column equalities, nonnegativity, and rational arc inequalities; row sums also bound every variable. A nonempty bounded rational polytope has a rational basic feasible solution. Cramer's rule and Hadamard's bound give polynomial bit length because the coefficient matrix has polynomial dimension and 0/1 entries and the right-hand sides are input rationals. The paths and weights form a polynomial-size certificate verifiable by exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: The facts q_st<=d_max and E[Y]=x are insufficient by themselves for arbitrary grouped incidence vectors.
claims.evidence: For two unit groups with three equiprobable row and column choices, every coordinate has expectation 1/3+1/3=2/3. Every integral row/column choice has value 2 at their intersection, hence discrepancy 2-2/3=4/3>d_max=1. The exact Fraction-based checker tested all 9 choices and obtained maximum discrepancy exactly 4/3 each time.
claims.search_method: Explicit finite construction plus exhaustive exact-rational evaluation.
claims.witness: Two groups of weight 1 on the 3-by-3 coordinates: group one chooses one complete row and group two chooses one complete column, each uniformly among three choices.

claims.claim: A dominant-path residual gives an exact, efficiently checkable sufficient condition for the target.
claims.evidence: Let the selected maximum-weight path have weight f_i* and residual r_i=q_i-f_i*. If it contains arc a, consolidation changes the group contribution by q_i-x_i,a, at most the total weight r_i of other paths. If it omits a, the original contribution x_i,a is entirely carried by other paths and is again at most r_i. The change is zero where all supported paths agree. Thus the triangle inequality gives |y_a-x_a|<=sum_{i:a in C_i}r_i, proving the stated certificate; all sets, maxima, sums, and comparisons are polynomially computable from the decomposition.
claims.search_method: Per-group signed discrepancy proof and complexity audit.

claims.claim: If every pair group has at most h supported paths and total supply B satisfies B<=h d_max/(h-1), the exact target holds; in particular, two-path groups suffice whenever B<=2d_max.
claims.evidence: For integer h>=2, a largest path has weight at least q_i/h, so r_i<=((h-1)/h)q_i. Since sum_i q_i=B, every residual certificate sum is at most ((h-1)/h)B<=d_max. Taking h=2 gives B<=2d_max. If h=1, every group is already supported on one path and y=x, so the conclusion is trivially true.
claims.search_method: Algebraic reduction to the verified dominant-path certificate, including the one-path edge case.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm producing an unsplittable y with max_a |y_a-x_a|<=min(B,sqrt((|V|-1)d_max B)).
claims.evidence: For independent group choices, with p_ia the probability that group i uses a, E[sum_a(Y_a-x_a)^2]=sum_{a,i}q_i^2p_ia(1-p_ia). Conditional expectation can fix each group to a supported path without increasing this exact rational potential. Dropping 1-p_ia, using q_i<=d_max, expected path length sum_a p_ia<=|V|-1, and sum_i q_i=B bounds the final potential by (|V|-1)d_max B. Each coordinate discrepancy is at most its square root. Separately x_a,y_a are both in [0,B], giving the simultaneous B bound. Enumerating supported choices and updating rational conditional expectations is polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Variance calculation, conditional-expectation derandomization, and bit-complexity audit.

claims.claim: An expected-polynomial-time exact sampler improves the general relaxed bound to max_a |y_a-x_a|<=sqrt(d_max B ceil(log_2(4|A|))/2).
claims.evidence: For each arc, Hoeffding applies to independent variables of ranges q_i, with sum_i q_i^2<=d_max B. For L=ceil(log_2(4|A|)) and lambda^2=d_max B L/2, the two-sided tail is at most 2e^{-L}. A union bound gives failure probability at most 2|A|e^{-L}<=2|A|2^{-L}<=1/2. Exact rejection testing of 2(y_a-x_a)^2<=d_max B L therefore takes at most two trials in expectation. Rational discrete path choices can be sampled exactly with expected polynomially many random bits and arithmetic operations.
claims.search_method: Exact Hoeffding-constant, union-bound, rejection-sampling, and bit-model audit.

claims.claim: If the positive-support digraph of x has at most one directed path for every ordered source-sink pair, then y=x is already unsplittable.
claims.evidence: Every path in a decomposition of x lies in its positive support. Under the hypothesis, all terms sharing endpoints must be the same path and can be merged by adding their weights. This leaves x unchanged and produces at most one path per ordered pair. In a DAG, capped path counts can be computed dynamically for every source-sink pair in polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Support-path uniqueness argument and DAG algorithm audit.

claims.claim: The exact target holds in polynomial time whenever there is only one sink.
claims.evidence: With one sink, total supply B equals d_max. Consolidate each source's decomposed flow onto any one of its supported paths to the sink. Endpoint balances are preserved and there is one path per source-sink pair. Both the original and consolidated flow on every arc lie in [0,B], so their absolute difference is at most B=d_max. Decomposition and consolidation are polynomial-time rational operations.
claims.search_method: Constructive single-sink proof with global-flow bound.

claims.claim: Integral lower-and-upper flow feasibility lemma: if an integral-balance flow g lies between integral arc bounds l and u, an integral flow z with the same balances and bounds exists and is computable in polynomial time.
claims.evidence: Subtract l, producing integral adjusted balances and integral capacities u-l. The assumed g-l is a feasible fractional bounded flow. The standard supersource/supersink reduction therefore has a fractional maximum flow of the required integral value; integral-capacity max-flow integrality supplies an integral one. Adding l back yields z with the original balances and bounds, and standard max-flow algorithms are polynomial in the bit model.
claims.search_method: Lower-bound reduction and max-flow integrality proof.

claims.claim: The exact target holds whenever b(v)/d_max is an integer for every vertex; this includes all single-source instances with equal sink demands.
claims.evidence: Set Delta=d_max and g=x/Delta. Its balances are integral. Applying the integral-bounds lemma with floor(g_a) and ceil(g_a) gives integral z, and y=Delta z differs from x by less than Delta on nonintegral coordinates and by zero on integral ones. For every sink, 0<d_t/Delta<=1 and this ratio is integral, so it equals 1. A unit-by-unit path decomposition of the integral acyclic z consequently has exactly one path ending at each sink, which precludes repeated ordered source-sink pairs. Equal-demand single-source instances satisfy the balance divisibility condition.
claims.search_method: Scaling, integral rounding, and unit path-decomposition proof.

claims.claim: For a single source and two sinks of scaled demands 1 and alpha<=1, there is a feasible integral two-unit flow z with lower bound 1 on H={a:x_a>1} and upper bound 1 on L={a:x_a<alpha}, with upper bound 2 elsewhere.
claims.evidence: Here alpha is positive. Split a path decomposition as x=f_1+f_2 by terminal sink and set g=f_1+f_2/alpha. This has balances +2,-1,-1. On H, g_a>=x_a>1, so it meets lower bound 1. On L, g_a<=x_a/alpha<1, so it meets upper bound 1. Each normalized component is a unit path flow, hence g_a<=2 everywhere. Thus g is a feasible fractional flow for the stated integral bounds, and the integral-bounds lemma supplies the required integral z in polynomial time.
claims.search_method: Normalized two-commodity decomposition and integral-bounds proof.

claims.claim: The exact target is computable in polynomial time for every single-source instance with at most two sinks, with arbitrary rational demands.
claims.evidence: For two sinks, decompose the integral two-unit z into one unit path ending at each sink and give them weights 1 and alpha. If z_a=0, the lower bound forces x_a<=1. If z_a=2, the upper bound on L forces x_a>=alpha, while path decomposition gives x_a<=1+alpha, so the error is at most 1. If z_a=1, y_a is 1 or alpha; over 0<=x_a<=1+alpha either choice differs by at most 1. Rescaling by the larger demand gives error at most d_max. The one-sink case was established separately, and every construction uses polynomial-time exact rational or integral-flow operations.
claims.search_method: Complete three-case discrepancy proof following integral path decomposition.

claims.claim: No counterexample exists in the finite SSUF classes exhaustively checked by exhaust_ssuf.py.
claims.evidence: The independent integer checker enumerates every forward-arc mask with one to three terminal suffix sinks, every scaled positive demand vector with maximum Q, every weak path-composition flow, and every one-path-per-sink candidate. It reproduced exactly 4,146,045 distinct checked flows for n<=6,Q<=3 and 168,336 for n<=5,Q<=5—the two reported totals—and found no violation of |y_a-x_a|<=Q. Matching both totals also identifies the intended finite classes rather than merely checking a coarser subset.
claims.search_method: Independent exhaustive integer enumeration via `python3 audit_exact_checks.py --verify-reported-ssuf`.

target_evidence: The exact target is universal over all rational acyclic b-transshipments. The draft explicitly says it has neither a proof nor a counterexample for that universal statement. It does prove material exact subclasses and certificates, notably one sink, balance divisibility, unique support paths, and every single-source instance with at most two sinks; it also gives valid but generally weaker discrepancy bounds. The row/column obstruction is expressly not a directed-graph counterexample, and finite enumeration cannot settle the universal target. General multi-source instances and single-source instances with at least three nonuniform sink demands remain uncovered. Therefore the work is VALID_PARTIAL_PROGRESS, not a full resolution. The draft's claimed_resolution is PARTIAL and its final writeup expressly limits its scope, so claimed_resolution is ACCURATE.
